days.title: Two Positions, One Root
days.intro: Everything in the Woodshed sits in two five-fret windows built from one root on the E string. Position 1 reaches forward from the root, up the neck. Position 2 reaches back from it. On a bass every string is a 4th apart, so the shapes never change from one string to the next, and inside a window every note has exactly one place.
do: Find C on the E string, 8th fret. The octave is two strings up and two frets up, on the D string, 10th fret. That octave and everything between is Position 1.
Same root. Now find the octave reaching back: G string, 5th fret. That's Position 2.
Go round the circle: C G D A E B F♯ D♭ A♭ E♭ B♭ F. Find each root on the E string, then play root to octave in Position 1 and in Position 2. Say the note name each time.
days.rule: One finger per fret. Four frets belong to your four fingers; the fifth fret of the window is a stretch, or a small shift if it's low on the neck.
days.got: You can find both octaves from any root on the E string without thinking about it.

days.title: Every Interval in Position 1
days.intro: Twelve notes in five frets. This is all of Position 1 before any mode is applied, and every mode in the Woodshed is a selection from it.
do: Drone on C. Play from the root up through all twelve intervals to the octave, one per beat, saying each one.
Then call intervals at random and find them: ♭3, 6, ♭7, 2, 5, ♭5, 7, 4.
Listen to each one against the drone. Some sit (5, 3, 8). Some lean (♭2, ♭5, 7).
days.rule: Say the interval before you play it, not after.
days.got: You can play any interval called out without counting up from the root.

days.title: Every Interval in Position 2
days.intro: The same twelve notes, reaching back from the root. Position 2 uses all four strings, and the root sits at the top of the window instead of the bottom.
do: Drone on C. Root up to the octave through all twelve, saying each interval.
Random intervals again, this time in Position 2: 3, ♭7, 6, ♭2, 4, 7, ♭3, 5.
Then alternate: an interval in Position 1, the same interval in Position 2.
days.rule: Keep your hand still. Every note is under a finger or one fret away.
days.got: Position 2 feels as familiar as Position 1.

days.title: The 3rds and the 5th
days.intro: The 3rd decides major or minor and the 5th holds the chord up. On bass you'll play these more than everything else put together. The 3 is filled, the ♭3 is hollow.
do: Drone on C. Root, 3, 5, 8 and back. Then root, ♭3, 5, 8.
Alternate root–3 and root–♭3, and hear major turn to minor with nothing else changing.
Both positions, then move the root round the circle and do it again.
days.rule: Keep the root on beat 1 every time.
days.got: You can hear whether a 3rd is major or minor before your hand gets there.

days.title: The 6th and the Two 7ths
days.intro: Three notes a semitone apart, and each one names a different chord: the 6 for 6 chords and Dorian minor, the ♭7 for dominant and minor 7th chords, the 7 for major 7ths. The ♭7 is hollow.
do: Root, 5, 6, ♭7, 7, 8 over the drone, slowly.
Root–♭7, then root–7, back to back: the dominant sound, then the major 7th sound.
In Position 2 the 7 is right under the octave on the G string. Find it without looking.
days.rule: Play each one against the root, not against the note before it.
days.got: You can tell a 6, a ♭7 and a 7 apart by sound against the drone.

days.title: The 2nds and 4ths
days.intro: The notes between the chord tones. The 2 and 4 are the passing notes most bass lines are made of. The ♭2 and ♭5 are the tense ones that Phrygian and Locrian are built on. The ♭2 and ♭5 are hollow.
do: Root, 2, 3 and back. Root, 4, 5 and back. These are the steps a walking line uses.
Then root, ♭2, root, and root, ♭5, 5. Listen to how much the ♭2 and ♭5 want to move.
Both positions.
days.rule: Every 2 or 4 has to step to a chord tone next.
days.got: You can play a step line from the root to the 5 and back in both positions without hesitating on the 2 or the 4.

days.title: The Major Triad
days.intro: 1, 3 and 5. Every major chord, and the frame every major mode hangs on. Position 2 is up at the 15th fret here because G on the 3rd fret has no room to reach back.
do: Drone on G. Play 1, 3, 5, 8 and back in Position 1, then Position 2.
Play the three inversions in the bottom row in order without stopping, then back down.
Start a bar on each triad note in turn and play the other two after it.
days.rule: Beat 1 is the root on the first pass, the 3 on the second, the 5 on the third.
days.got: You can start the triad from any of its notes in either position without finding the root first.

days.title: The Minor Triad
days.intro: 1, ♭3 and 5. One note different from major, and that note is the whole difference in sound.
do: Drone on G. Play 1, ♭3, 5, 8 and back in Position 1, then Position 2.
Play the three inversions in the bottom row in order without stopping, then back down.
Alternate a bar of major and a bar of minor, moving only the 3rd.
days.rule: Move one finger only when you switch between major and minor.
days.got: You can switch major to minor on any inversion without stopping.

days.title: The Diminished Triad
days.intro: 1, ♭3 and ♭5: two minor 3rds stacked. You'll meet it as the bottom of a m7♭5 chord and inside Locrian.
do: Drone on G. Play 1, ♭3, ♭5, 8 and back in Position 1, then Position 2.
Play the three inversions in the bottom row in order without stopping, then back down.
Play it against a minor triad: only the 5th moves, down a fret.
days.rule: Always resolve the ♭5: down to the 4 or up to the 5.
days.got: The diminished triad sounds like a chord to you, not a mistake.

days.title: The Augmented Triad
days.intro: 1, 3 and ♯5: two major 3rds stacked. Every note is the same distance from the next, so each inversion is the same shape moved up.
do: Drone on G. Play 1, 3, ♯5, 8 and back in Position 1, then Position 2.
Play the three inversions in the bottom row in order without stopping, then back down.
Play it against the major triad: only the 5th moves, up a fret.
days.rule: Resolve the ♯5 up to the 6 or back down to the 5.
days.got: You can hear the ♯5 pulling upward.

days.title: One Note Apart
days.intro: The four triads are one triad with a note moved. Major to minor moves the 3rd. Minor to diminished moves the 5th down. Major to augmented moves the 5th up. The hollow note is where you start; the ringed note is where it goes.
do: Drone on G. Play each pair as two bars: four beats of the first triad, four of the second.
Then chain them: major, minor, diminished, minor, major, augmented, major.
Do the same chain from the 1st inversion.
days.rule: Only the moving finger moves.
days.got: You can name which triad you're playing from the sound alone, with the drone on.

days.title: Triads to Sevenths
days.intro: Add a 7th to a triad and you have the five seventh chords a bass player meets every day. Major triad plus 7 is maj7, plus ♭7 is a dominant 7. Minor plus ♭7 is m7. Diminished plus ♭7 is m7♭5; plus ♭♭7 (the 6) is dim7.
do: Drone on G. Play each chord 1 to 8 and back, then 8 down to 1 and back.
Go through all five without stopping, one bar each.
Then just the top note: play the triad and land on the 7th. Hear how each 7th changes the chord.
days.rule: Say the chord name as you play its first note.
days.got: You can play any of the five from the root when someone names it.

days.title: The Map: D Ionian
days.sub: The major scale. Every other mode in the Woodshed is this one with something changed.
days.intro: It's the parent key itself. Over the I chord in a major key: major, maj7 and 6 chords. The root is white and the colour note, 7, has the double ring. Every page this week uses these two shapes; only what's lit changes.
days.after: D Ionian: D E F♯ G A B C♯
do: Drone on D. Play Position 1 from the root to the octave and back, saying each interval as you play it.
Same in Position 2. Then alternate: one bar in each position, without stopping.
Listen for the 4. It's the one note that rubs against the chord, so pass through it rather than sitting on it.
days.rule: Never start on the root. Start each run on a different note of the pattern.
days.got: You can name the interval under any finger without counting up from the root.

days.title: The Triad: D Major
days.intro: The triad inside the mode. The rest of the pattern stays faint, so you see the triad as part of the mode, not a separate shape. The bottom row is the three inversions in Position 1; the last one reaches above the octave onto the G string.
do: Drone on D. Triad up and down in each position, saying the intervals.
Play the inversions in order without stopping, then back down. Then start each bar on a different inversion.
Between each triad note, play the faint note just above it. That's the triad with the mode filled in.
days.rule: Land on a different triad note on beat 1 of each bar.
days.got: You can start the triad from any of its notes in either position without finding the root first.

days.title: The Seventh: Dmaj7
days.intro: Add the 7 to the triad and it becomes Dmaj7. Same shape. Start the same arpeggio from the 3 and carry it up to the 9, and you have F♯m7: a seventh chord sitting inside Dmaj7. Playing it over D gives you the 9 without leaving the chord.
do: Drone on D. Arpeggio up and down in each position: 1 to 8 and back, then 8 down to 1 and back.
Play it from the 3: 3 5 7 8, then back down to the 3.
Then four notes a bar in a different order each bar, without repeating an order.
days.rule: Arpeggio notes only. If you play a faint note, start the bar again.
days.got: You can play the arpeggio in any order at a steady tempo without looking at the page.

days.title: The Colour: the 7
days.sub: What makes Ionian sound like Ionian
days.intro: The 7 is what separates Ionian from Mixolydian. It sits a semitone under the octave and pulls up into it. Flatten it and you're in Mixolydian. The rule for the week: triad notes on the beat, the colour note between them.
do: Two notes, one bar: the 8 on beat 1, the 7 on the ‘and’ of 2, back to the 8 on 3. Then swap the pair for the 5 and the 7.
Then a bar of quarter notes: a triad note on 1 and 3, the 7 on 2 or 4. Move the triad notes around; keep the colour off the strong beats.
Turn the drone off for the last two minutes and play the same thing. If it still sounds like the mode, you've got it.
days.rule: The 7 never lands on beat 1.
days.got: You can hear which mode you're in from the 7 alone.

days.title: The Move: Two Strings, Six Notes
days.intro: Three notes on the E string and the next three on the A string. That six-note block is how you get round the neck without whole-neck shapes. Slide it along the neck to start on the 2 and the same notes become Dorian. Move it across to the A and D strings, starting on the 4, and you land on Lydian: one step brighter. The filled note is where each block starts.
do: Play the root block up and back. Then slide up a block, and keep going up the neck through all seven, naming each mode as you land.
Come back down the same way. Then go back to the root block and move it across a string.
Drone on D throughout: every block is still D Ionian, whatever mode name it has from its own first note.
days.rule: Three notes on every string, even where it stretches.
days.got: You can start a block on any note of the mode and name its mode before you play it.

days.title: The Line: I–vi–ii–V
days.intro: A I–vi–ii–V turnaround. All four chords come from D major, so the whole line stays in this one pattern. One bar per diagram, four quarter notes. The small numbers are the beats; the order is also under each diagram. The chord's root is white, its other chord tones filled, passing notes hollow.
do: Play it slowly with a backing loop of the chords, or a drone on the root if you have no loop. Start around 70 bpm.
Four times through reading, four times without the page.
Then keep beats 1 and 3 as they are and change beats 2 and 4. Notes from the pattern only.
days.rule: Beat 1 is the chord's root. Beat 3 is a chord tone. Beat 4 steps into the next bar.
days.got: You can play it without the page, then make up a second version that follows the same rule.

Then a bar of quarter notes: a triad note on 1 and 3, the 6 on 2 or 4. Move the triad notes around; keep the colour off the strong beats.
Turn the drone off for the last two minutes and play the same thing. If it still sounds like the mode, you've got it.

days.intro: Move a block across one string at the same frets and it starts on the 4th: one step brighter, Ionian to Lydian. Move it across again and it would start on the ♭7, which isn't in the key, so one note shifts a fret. That shift is where brightness wraps round from Lydian to Locrian.

rows.figcap: E and A: from the root, Ionian
A and D: from the 4, Lydian

do: Drone on B♭. Play the root block, then the block one string over, without moving your hand along the neck.
Find the block on the D and G strings above them, and the one note that has to move.
Play all three as one phrase, bottom to top.
days.rule: Your hand only moves across, not along.
days.got: You can move up through the strings in one area without losing the key.

days.title: Where the Two Positions Sit
days.intro: The whole key from the 1st to the 15th fret. The shaded bands are the windows you know: Position 2 from the E string at the 6th fret (2–6), Position 1 from the same root (6–10), and Position 1 from the A string at the 13th fret (13–17 is off the page). Blocks join them up.
do: Drone on B♭. Play Position 2, then Position 1, one after the other.
Then join them with a block: start in Position 2, cross the root, carry on in Position 1.
Find the next B♭ up (E string, 18th fret, or A string, 13th) and work out which window it starts.
days.rule: Always know which window you're in.
days.got: You can travel from one end of the area to the other without stopping to find the key.

days.title: The Line: Up the Neck
days.intro: Four chords up the scale, each played in the block that starts on its root. The line climbs the neck one block per bar. Labels are from B♭; the faint notes are the rest of each block.
do: Slowly, around 70 bpm. Then come back down: E♭maj7, Dm7, Cm7, B♭maj7, in the same blocks.
Carry on up: Fsus, Gm7, Am7♭5, each in its own block.
Then the same idea on the A and D strings.
days.rule: One block per bar.
days.got: You can climb and descend the whole key with a chord a bar.

days.title: F Ionian Without Moving
days.sub: Fmaj7 in the F major area
days.intro: Fmaj7 is chord I of F major, so F Ionian is already under your hand in the F major area at the 1st fret. On the left it's labelled from F, with the chord tones lit; the colour note, 7, is one of them. On the right is the same mode in Position 2, for comparison. Same notes, different fingers.
do: Drone on F. Play every note of the F area from the lowest F to the highest and back, saying intervals from F.
Play the Fmaj7 arpeggio in the area, then add the 7 between chord tones.
Switch to the pattern on the right and play the same thing. Then back.
days.rule: The drone is F, not F. Hear everything from F.
days.got: The F area sounds like F Ionian when the drone is on F.

days.title: D Aeolian and E Locrian Without Moving
days.sub: Dm7 and Em7♭5 in the F major area
days.intro: The last two. Dm7 is the vi chord and Em7♭5 the vii, so D Aeolian and E Locrian are in the same area too. That's all seven modes in five frets: the parent key is the map, and the drone decides which mode you hear.
do: Drone on D. The area from D to D, then the Dm7 arpeggio with the ♭6 between chord tones.
Drone on E. The same with Em7♭5 and the ♭5.
Then change the drone every two bars through all seven roots, F to E, and keep playing in the same five frets.
days.rule: Your hand stays at the 1st fret all session.
days.got: You can hear all seven modes from one position just by changing the drone.

days.title: Where the Roots Are
days.sub: Twelve keys between the 1st and 10th frets
days.intro: This week every mode goes round all twelve keys without leaving the first ten frets. The rule for choosing a position: find the root on the E string. Up to the 4th fret (teal), use Position 1. From the 5th fret up (white), use Position 2. E♭ and E aren't on the E string in that range, so take them from the A string, 6th and 7th frets, in Position 1 (hollow).

rows.cap: Roots on the E and A strings, 1st to 10th fret

do: Go round the circle, C F B♭ E♭ A♭ D♭ G♭ B E A D G, and for each root say the fret and the position before you play it.
Then play root to octave in that position for each key, one bar each.
Then the major triad in each key, one bar each, round the whole circle.
days.rule: Decide the position before you move.
days.got: You can go round all twelve keys without a pause at the change.

days.title: Ionian Round the Circle
days.sub: C F B♭ E♭ A♭ D♭ G♭ B E A D G
days.intro: Ionian in all twelve keys, staying between the 1st and 10th frets. The first two keys are drawn: C in Position 2 from the 8th fret, and F in Position 1 from the 1st. After that, use the root map from Day 169.
do: Drone on each root in turn. Two bars of Ionian in each key, root to octave and back, then move on round the circle.
Second time round: one bar each, and land on the 7 on beat 3.
Third time: no drone. Say the key name as you arrive.
days.rule: Never stop at a key change. If you get lost, play the root and keep going.
days.got: You can go round the circle in Ionian with no gaps.

do: Slowly, around 70 bpm, reading.
From memory, four times.
Then carry on round the circle: A♭maj7, D♭maj7, G♭maj7 and on, with the same idea in each bar.
days.rule: Beat 4 steps into the next key.

days.title: From Chord Symbol to Pattern
days.sub: The last week: everything at once
days.intro: Every page in the Woodshed comes down to one question: what's the chord, and which mode goes with it? This is the whole answer on one page. Once you have the mode, you have the pattern, and the triad, seventh, colour note and line are all inside it.
days.after:
ChordFirst choiceWhen it's something else
maj7, 6IonianLydian on the IV chord, or wherever the 4 clashes
m7DorianAeolian on the vi or the i of a minor key; Phrygian on the iii
7MixolydianLydian dominant if it doesn't resolve down a 5th; altered or Phrygian dominant if it resolves to a minor chord
m7♭5LocrianLocrian ♮2 when the melody has a natural 9
m6, m(maj7)Melodic minorHarmonic minor on the i of a minor key with its V7 nearby
7♭9Phrygian dominantAltered if the melody has a ♯9 or ♯5
do: Take a lead sheet you don't know. For every chord, say the mode before you play anything.
Play the root and the colour note of each mode, one bar per chord.
Then the line rule from the Day 6 pages: root on 1, chord tone on 3, approach on 4.
days.rule: Name the mode before the first note of every chord.
days.got: You can play through a tune you've never seen and know which pattern you're in at every bar.

days.title: One Dominant, Four Patterns
days.intro: Four modes over the same G7, each with its chord tones lit and the note that sets it apart ringed. Mixolydian if the chord stays put, Lydian dominant if it moves without resolving down a 5th, altered if it resolves with tension, Phrygian dominant if it resolves to a minor chord.
do: Drone on G. Two bars of each mode in turn.
Then play each one resolving: Mixolydian to C, Lydian dominant staying on G, altered to C, Phrygian dominant to Cm.
Hear which resolution each one wants.
days.rule: Chord tones on the beat, colour note off it.
days.got: You can choose the mode for a G7 from where it's going.

days.title: One Minor 7th, Three Patterns
days.intro: Dorian, Aeolian and Phrygian all fit Gm7. The difference is the colour: the 6 for the ii chord, the ♭6 for the vi or the i of a minor key, the ♭2 for the iii.
do: Drone on G. Two bars of each.
Play a Dorian line, then play it again changing only the 6 to ♭6.
Then change the 2 to ♭2. Three moods from one note at a time.
days.rule: Change one note at a time.
days.got: You can hear which minor mode is which with your eyes shut.

days.title: Major and Half-Diminished
days.intro: The last two decisions. Ionian or Lydian on a maj7, and Locrian or Locrian ♮2 on a m7♭5. In each pair one note changes.
do: Drone on G. Ionian then Lydian, listening to the 4 move.
Then Locrian and Locrian ♮2, listening to the 2 move.
Make a phrase that uses the changing note on the off-beat and play it both ways.
days.rule: The changing note goes off the beat.
days.got: You can hear the difference between each pair from one note.

days.title: Seven Modes, One Root
days.intro: The seven major modes on one root, in scale order: Ionian, Dorian, Phrygian, Lydian, Mixolydian, Aeolian, Locrian. Each one is its Week 3–9 map moved to G, with the colour note ringed.
do: Drone on G. One bar of each mode, root to octave and back, without stopping between them.
Then brightest to darkest: Lydian, Ionian, Mixolydian, Dorian, Aeolian, Phrygian, Locrian. One note changes each time.
Then just the colour notes: root, colour, root, for each mode.
days.rule: Say the mode name on beat 1 of its bar.
days.got: You can play all seven on one root without looking.

days.title: The Line: Everything at Once
days.intro: A ii–V–I–VI in G with a chromatic approach into every bar. Each bar is labelled from its own chord, and the E7 bar uses G♯ from E Phrygian dominant. The dashed rings are the chromatic notes: outside the pattern for one beat, on the way into the next chord.
do: Slowly, around 70 bpm. Then from memory.
Write a second chorus with the same rules: root on 1, chord tone on 3, approach on 4.
Then play eight bars with no plan, alternating your two versions with whatever comes.
days.rule: Beat 4 is always a semitone or a step from the next root.
days.got: You can walk through the changes for a whole chorus without stopping.

days.title: Lap Two
days.intro: That's the 26 weeks. The Woodshed is built to run again, and the second lap is different from the first without a single new page.
do: New keys. Every week moves two steps round the circle: Week 1 in D instead of C, Week 3 in E instead of D, and so on. Twenty-six weeks is two more than two full turns of the circle, so each lap lands every week in new keys.
Faster. Add 10 bpm to every Day 6 line, and play it from memory before you look at the page.
From the A string. On the Map pages, play Position 1 from the A string as well as the E string.
Your own lines. On every Day 6, write your own line first, then compare it with the one on the page.
Review days stay. They're where the earlier pages come back, and they're what keeps lap one from fading.
days.rule: Same page, new key.
days.got: You can open the Woodshed at any page, in any key, and play it.
